title: Bollinger Band Width Squeeze on BTC — Volatility Expansion Breakout
objective: Research whether Bollinger Band Width contraction (squeeze) followed by a directional breakout produces profitable entries on BTC 1h candles. Hypothesis: periods of low volatility (narrow BB width) precede explosive directional moves; entering on bandwidth expansion with a momentum filter identifies these early. This is a VOLATILITY strategy, distinct from the mean-reversion BB already tested on ETH. Parameters: BB period 20, BB std 2.0, width lookback 20, squeeze threshold 0.1–0.3 (optimized), entry on width expansion breakout with 20-period momentum confirmation. Stop-loss: 2x ATR, no fixed TP (ride until momentum flips). Test on 6+ months BTCUSDT 1h data via WFA with Optuna (50–100 trials).

title: Multi-Timeframe EMA Trend Gate on ETH — Regime-Filtered RSI Pullback
objective: Test EMA Trend Gate strategy (4h EMA regime filter + 1h RSI pullback entries) on 7.5yr ETHUSDT 1h data. Real WFA completed: 85 windows, 1216 trades, Sharpe 0.528, max DD -16.37%. Result: partial (below 0.8 Sharpe gate). See EXP-20260321200000-01.

title: Multi-Timeframe EMA Confluence with Trend Strength Gate on BTC
objective: Research whether filtering 1h RSI entries by 4h EMA trend direction improves Sharpe over pure RSI on BTC 1h candles. Hypothesis: Entries only when 4h EMA slope confirms direction reduce false signals from oscillating RSI in trendless markets, improving Sharpe from ~0.94 to >1.1 on OOS data. Test via WFA with Optuna optimization on 6+ months of BTCUSDT 1h data.

title: Volatility Contraction-Expansion Regime Strategy on Full BTC Dataset
objective: Test the existing volatility_regime strategy (multi-timeframe: 1h with 4h regime detection) on the full 6481-candle BTCUSDT dataset (~9 months) via proper WFA with Optuna. Hypothesis: volatility contraction followed by expansion produces directional breakouts that can be traded profitably. This is a fundamentally different signal class from price-based RSI/SMA/Bollinger strategies already tested.

title: Multi-Timeframe EMA Trend Gate on BTC/USDT
objective: Test a regime-filtered pullback strategy: use 4h EMA slope to detect market regime (uptrend/downtrend), then enter 1h pullback trades only in the direction of the 4h trend. Strategy is long-only in uptrends, short-only in downtrends. RSI confirms entries. ATR-based stops. Use full available BTC 1h history via Binance API fetch, then run WFA with Optuna optimization. This is a fundamentally different strategy class (multi-timeframe regime-detection) from all prior experiments (RSI, SMA, BB, spreads).

title: BB Width Squeeze on BTC Deep Data
objective: Test the BB Width Squeeze volatility expansion breakout strategy on 5 years of BTCUSDT hourly data (2021-2026). Strategy: Bollinger Band width contraction (squeeze) precedes explosive directional moves; enter on bandwidth expansion breakout with momentum confirmation. This is different from Bollinger Bands mean-reversion (tested on ETH) which uses price at band extremes - BB Width uses VOLATILITY contraction as the leading indicator. Test via WFA with Optuna optimization (100 trials, 3mo train/1mo test/1mo step).

title: MACD Divergence with RSI Filter on BTC — Momentum Reversal Strategy
objective: Research MACD histogram divergence from price (hidden bullish/bearish divergence) combined with RSI oversold/overbought filter for entry confirmation on BTC 1h candles. Hypothesis: MACD divergence signals early trend exhaustion, and RSI filter (below 40 for longs, above 60 for shorts) filters false signals, producing higher Sharpe than pure RSI (0.94) on BTC. This is a DIFFERENT signal class from price-based RSI/SMA/Bollinger/BBand Width - uses MACD momentum divergence + RSI confluence. Test on maximum available BTC history (5+ years of 1h data) via WFA with Optuna optimization (100 trials, 3mo train/1mo test/1mo step).

title: BB-KC Squeeze Breakout on BTC — Pure Numpy Volatility Expansion Strategy
objective: Research whether Bollinger Bands contracting inside Keltner Channels (BB-KC squeeze) followed by BB exiting KC produces profitable breakout signals on BTC 1h candles. Hypothesis: volatility compression (BB inside KC) followed by expansion (BB exits KC) precedes explosive directional moves with higher Sharpe than mean-reversion or pure momentum strategies. Key difference from existing BB Width Squeeze: this uses SPATIAL band relationships (BB vs KC), not bandwidth percentage. Pure numpy implementation avoids pandas dependency entirely. Test on 5 years of binance_btcusdt_1h_deep.csv (43K+ candles, 2021-2026) via WFA with Optuna (100 trials, 3mo train/1mo test/1mo step) using the full WFA engine.

title: Volatility-Adaptive Supertrend on BTC — Dynamic Position Sizing with ATR
objective: Test Volatility-Adaptive Supertrend strategy on 5 years of BTCUSDT 1h data (43K+ bars). Hypothesis: position size inversely scaled by 20-bar ATR% (lower size in high-vol regimes) combined with Supertrend crossovers reduces maximum drawdown vs fixed-size strategies while maintaining positive Sharpe. Strategy is fundamentally different from all prior experiments: (1) position sizing is dynamic, not fixed; (2) Supertrend signal is different from RSI/SMA/BB price-based signals; (3) addresses the drawdown concern that plagued ATR Breakout (-5.0 Sharpe) and London Sweep (-4.997 Sharpe). Asset: BTCUSDT on full 5-year deep dataset. Run via full WFA engine (Optuna, 100 trials, 3mo train/1mo test/1mo step) with realistic costs.

title: ETH Session Momentum: Europe-to-US Continuation
objective: Research and backtest whether strong ETH hourly returns during the European trading session (08:00–16:00 UTC) predict continued momentum into the US trading session (14:00–22:00 UTC). The mechanism: 24/7 crypto markets lack the overnight MM hedging pressure that causes intraday reversal in equities, so institutional orders carry momentum across sessions. Use WFA with Optuna on the existing 7.5-year ETH 1h dataset (64k+ candles) to find the optimal momentum threshold and holding period. Test on ETH/USDT Binance perpetual data.

title: Realized Volatility-Adaptive RSI on ETH
objective: Test a realized volatility-adaptive position sizing strategy on ETH 1h candles. Position size scales inversely with 20-period realized volatility, targeting ~10% annualized portfolio volatility. Trades are taken on RSI pullback signals (RSI < oversold threshold) with ATR-based stops/targets. The core hypothesis: volatility-adaptive sizing will improve risk-adjusted returns vs fixed sizing by automatically reducing exposure during high-vol regimes and increasing it during calm periods. Test on 7.5-year ETHUSDT history (64,733 bars already present) via full WFA with Optuna optimization over 5 parameters.
